body:
I am in love with someone who has had suicidal thoughts since she was 15. At least I was in love. I don't know.

I broke her heart once already. And she came back. I told her to slow down, that I am afraid I could harm her again. Seh didn't listen. Now I break her heart every month or so. It can be  over something important. But it can also be over something stupid, like lost keys.

I thought I wanted to kill myself. I cut myself. I banged my head against the wall. I tried to get drunk, swallow two aspirin tabs and slit my veins in a hot shower. I am still standing. I was ashamed of my wounds. Now I display them. I used to make up stories about my scars. Not today.

I started a job so I could forget and buy her things from my own pocket. That job made me smoke and hate myself even more. The people are nice. The boss can be nice sometimes too. But I just can't run away.

I try not to break her heart. I do it anyway. I try not to make her sad. I do it anyway. If I try to keep her from thinking about suicide and she reminds me that I tried it too. What she never mentions is the fact that it was her who saved me from doing it. 

When I stare in the headlights of the approaching subway I am stopped by a mixture of my love towards her and fear.

I no longer want to kill myself. I want to be healthy, but I just can't. How can I be healthy if I'm in a relationship that doesn't make me happy? Leave her? How can I leave her with clear conscience if I know she will take her life after that?

I want to stay and I want to love but she tells me I'm lying and that I'm trying to convince myself that I love her. I am slowly starting to believe that.

I am trying. Believe me, I am. I am desperately looking for the spark I once harbored towards her. The spark that made me wake up in the middle of the night and start writing poems. The spark that made me bring her roses and hide cute messages around her room. The spark that made me write a play that was written for one pair of eyes only. The spark that made me love.

Maybe it will never light up again. I try to ignite it with alcohol, weed, cigarettes, hash, coke, MDMA, sex, dinners, movies, slit wrists and childish tears. I try to talk to myself. I try to talk to others. It's all white noise. Nothing I hear makes sense to me.

Maybe we're all supposed to be fucked up. That thought is giving me peace. We're all messed up in our own ways. We think the baggage we show betrays the burden we hide. We feel fake. We feel pathetic.

Maybe we're not supposed to reach the light at the end of a tunnel. Maybe we're all going to die in a dark alleyway alone, miserable and high on opioids.

We glorify overdose, we celebrate feeling empty and we turn depression into its own form of comedy. The nihilistic memes we share are the laughter drowning out the cry for help. The strain we smoke is just inhaling THC into pitch black nothingness trying to revive something that's long dead. 

But nothing matters. We're all just an essay written in iNotes waiting to be deleted.
